title: A connected review, from evidence to follow-up
description: Connect bank-disclosure research, dollar-funding context and market-liquidity evidence through public pages, MCP and source-history APIs.

products.name: Undertow
products.owns: Market depth and size-specific exit evidence

capabilities.title: Keep missing evidence in the review
capabilities.description: Inspect source-dated changes, overdue fields and visibility gaps across tracked banks and lenders. Open the live review queue and its original disclosures.
capabilities.boundary: Review alerts require human assessment. They do not establish institutional safety or change model scores.

capabilities.title: Connect research to your AI workflow
capabilities.description: Use public MCP and REST, Financial Evidence Python 0.1.13 or AI SDK 0.1.2 to save cited reviews, compare later captures and build repeatable agent research.
capabilities.boundary: Each source keeps its dates, rights and missingness. Operator checks do not establish customer adoption.

capabilities.title: Ask for the funding evidence you need
capabilities.description: Seiche 0.16.5 provides compact funding context and exact metric retrieval, with compatible diagnostics, units and source dates retained.
capabilities.boundary: Package publication is separate from the hosted runtime identity and the freshness of each observation. Funding context does not authorize execution.

capabilities.title: Inspect what moves together
capabilities.description: Inspect shared-factor concentration and rolling correlations in the hosted NoiseFloor 0.4.0 workbench. Python/MCP 0.4.2 adds clearer input guidance with unchanged calculations.
capabilities.boundary: Noise analysis supplies research context. It does not grant feed rights, validate predictions or authorize a trade.

capabilities.title: Rehearse the controls around an action
capabilities.description: Explore the paper workbench: inspect refusals, duplicate protection, STOP and reconciliation before considering an execution workflow.
capabilities.boundary: The workbench is a simulation. Source permissions, freshness and account controls remain separate execution requirements.

capabilities.title: Retrieve dated source histories
capabilities.description: Read funding histories, bank filings and Bitcoin or Liquid settlement observations through the shared source-data API and MCP. Keep units, observation dates and capture times attached.
capabilities.boundary: Captured vintages begin with the archive. An as-known-at query cannot reconstruct observations before the first capture; missing values are not zero.

capabilities.title: Receive source-status updates
capabilities.description: Use reusable MCP sessions and bounded source-status updates. Clients retain expiry, source clocks, rights and missingness when a connection resets.
capabilities.action: Read the client and status-stream guide
capabilities.boundary: The stream reports scheduled source-status metadata. It is not a tick feed, complete replay history, execution-ready input or an availability guarantee.

capabilities.title: Separate bank updates from filings
capabilities.description: Review provisional business updates beside accepted filings, with distinct reporting and publication dates. Compare only the fields and periods the source actually discloses.
capabilities.boundary: A provisional update is not an audited financial result. Missing asset-quality or capital measures remain unavailable; the view does not certify bank safety.

capabilities.title: Inspect public agent activity evidence
capabilities.description: Browse selected agent registries, service catalogs and protocol events, with source and collection dates. Review what each observation can establish.
capabilities.boundary: Registrations, wallets, services and event logs are different units. They do not establish unique autonomous agents, customers, revenue or a complete global market. Private integrations require separate authorization.

limits: Coverage remains specific to each jurisdiction and market.
Funding conditions and market depth do not measure an institution’s deposit liquidity.
Release dates do not establish the freshness of source observations.
Evidence collection, delivery, validation and customer use are separate claims.
